column1: # Authored external identities for the ECMA-262 census, in the URL lane's
# format: one identity per line, every one namespaced `ext.`. A duplicate
# fails; an identity no dependency uses fails; a dependency naming an identity
# These are dependency names with a pin and no obligation to model. They are
# not unconstrained executable callbacks, and declaring one grants no coverage
# state to any row that names it.
# The namespaces are the escape treatments of rulings R-P6, R-P9 and R-P11.
# survey these are read from, group by group.
# --- The named ES2026 core boundary (R-P6 group A, B, C and H) --------------
# R-P9: recording an escaping reference here fixes only where it is written
# down, never a disposition. The completion discipline is reproduced by the
# model as an `Except`-shaped result and no in-scope row is `foreignBoundary`
# sec-normalcompletion, sec-throwcompletion, sec-completion-ao, and the `?` and
# Abstract Closures and function creation: sec-abstract-closure and
# sec-createbuiltinfunction, which carries the SetFunctionName and
# SetFunctionLength bookkeeping. Thirteen closures are created in scope and
# eleven are wrapped; the closures stay owned as first-order descriptors and
# only the object allocation and the name/length bookkeeping are host plumbing.
# The object model. These reach arbitrary user code, which is the decision-kind
# treatment AGENTS.md already mandates for a foreign boundary; their answers
# enter the tape as a returned value, a synchronous throw, or a promise
# The List and Record specification types (sec-list-and-record-specification-type).
# --- The iterator tape (R-P11, survey group D) ------------------------------
# Used only by the four combinators, four call sites each. The combinators
# consume a sequence of iterator answers — next value, done, throw — that is
# structurally identical to a Streams foreign-boundary answer tape, which is
# what keeps the combinator rows owned without inheriting all of clause 27.1.
# --- Intrinsics and well-known symbols (R-P11, survey group F) --------------
# An opaque enumeration of intrinsic names with an identity relation and no
# behaviour. %Promise% and %Promise.prototype% also carry `term` rows in scope,
# Nine in-scope steps throw a TypeError and two create an AggregateError. The
# model carries a throw completion tagged with an error kind and a reason
# value; it never constructs an Error object.
# --- The conventions record (R-P11, survey group H) -------------------------
# The nine `~enum~` spellings observed in scope, the `<< ... >>` List literal
# notation (44 pairs, U+00AB and U+00BB), and annex D's host layering points,
# recorded so a later reader can see the host hooks were enumerated and checked
# --- Agents, realms and execution contexts (R-P6 externals, survey group E) -
# DB-03 makes the queue state; it does not make the realm and active-script
# bookkeeping state. Nothing in mask M1 or M2 observes a realm, and every
# in-scope algorithm carries [[Realm]] opaquely through a job.
# --- In-family hooks named but not called (R-P11, survey group I) -----------

# sec-jobs prose but defined outside scope and called by no in-scope algorithm;
